note: HAND-AUTHORED, not model output. Written from the deterministic synthesis input of the Pricing scenario after the customer evidence was approved (as-of 2026-10-01). The experiment is kept inconclusive (c2, c3). Claim c6 is an INJECTED 'no harm' claim that reads an inconclusive, underpowered result as safety: the Reviewer fixture flags it.

claims.text: Conversion for Canadian signups on or after 2026-04-01 is 27.7% against 38.9% before, a difference of -11.2% (95% CI -14.3% to -8.1%) in an observational comparison.
The price test shows an effect of -0.0204 on conversion with a 95% CI from -0.0752 to +0.0343, so the result is inconclusive.
The test has a design power of 0.11 at the pre-registered MDE, so it could not reliably detect a conversion loss of that size.
1,126 relevant feedback mentions say the premium price is too high.
821 relevant feedback mentions say premium is worth the price.
The price test found no harm to conversion from the higher price.

uncertainties.text: The price test is underpowered, so its confidence interval spans both a loss and a gain.

gaps.text: No financial evidence exists for the revenue effect of the price change.

sections.summary: The price test is inconclusive [[c2]]. The observational comparison for one country shows lower conversion after the change date [[c1]]. Customers disagree about the price [[c4]] [[c5]].
